atoms.text: This guide configures access for the FrameForge transcoding service, which reads mezzanine video files from the bucket media-masters-prod and writes MP4 renditions back under the prefix renditions/. The bucket and the service's execution role, frameforge-transcode-role, belong to the same account, 111122223333. Access is granted only through the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not changed. In the IAM console, open the role and attach an inline policy with a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/masters/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/renditions/*. Add a third statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod with an s3:prefix condition of masters/*, so the service can enumerate input files. Because the role and the bucket share an account, no bucket policy statement is needed and the existing bucket policy stays as it is. To verify, submit a test job with a 10-second source clip and confirm that the output object appears under renditions/ with a nonzero size. If the job fails with AccessDenied, check the resource ARNs in the inline policy for typos.

This guide configures access for the FrameForge transcoding service, which reads mezzanine video files from the bucket media-masters-prod and writes MP4 renditions back under the prefix renditions/. The bucket is owned by account 111122223333, while the service's execution role, frameforge-transcode-role, runs in a different account, 444455556666. Access is granted by the bucket owner through a new statement in the bucket policy that names arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/frameforge-transcode-role as the principal. In the bucket owner's account, edit the bucket policy and add a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/masters/* for that principal. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod/renditions/*. Add a third statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::media-masters-prod with an s3:prefix condition of masters/*, so the service can enumerate input files. Because the bucket crosses an account boundary, the grant lives in the bucket policy rather than in the role's own policy. To verify, submit a test job with a 10-second source clip and confirm that the output object appears under renditions/ with a nonzero size. If the job fails with AccessDenied, check the principal ARN in the bucket policy for typos.

This guide covers access for the ScanLift OCR service, which reads scanned PDF files from the bucket records-intake-prod and writes extracted text as JSON to the prefix ocr-output/. The bucket and the service role, scanlift-ocr-role, are in the same account, 222233334444. The grant is made only in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Open the role in IAM and attach a managed policy whose first statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-intake-prod/scans/*. A second statement should allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-intake-prod/ocr-output/*. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, because the service never removes source scans after processing. Since the resources are in the same account, the identity-based policy is sufficient and no bucket policy edit is required. Test by uploading a three-page scanned PDF to scans/ and checking that a JSON file with the same base name appears under ocr-output/. If the output is missing, review the service's job logs for the AccessDenied error and compare the failing ARN with the policy.

This guide covers access for the ScanLift OCR service, which reads scanned PDF files from the bucket records-intake-prod and writes extracted text as JSON to the prefix ocr-output/. The bucket is owned by account 222233334444, and the service role, scanlift-ocr-role, belongs to a separate account, 555566667777. The grant is made by the bucket owner in a bucket policy statement that names account 555566667777 as the principal. In the owner's account, add a statement to the bucket policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-intake-prod/scans/* for arn:aws:iam::555566667777:root. A second statement should allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-intake-prod/ocr-output/* for the same principal. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, because the service never removes source scans after processing. Since the bucket is owned by a different account, the bucket policy carries the grant and the role's own policy is not the point of control. Test by uploading a three-page scanned PDF to scans/ and checking that a JSON file with the same base name appears under ocr-output/. If the output is missing, review the service's job logs for the AccessDenied error and compare the failing ARN with the policy.

This guide sets up access for the PixelSpan thumbnail service, which reads original JPEG and PNG images from the bucket catalog-images-prod and writes resized thumbnails to the prefix thumbs/. The bucket and the service role, pixelspan-resize-role, are both in account 333344445555. Access is provided only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not touched. Attach an inline policy to the role with s3:GetObject permission on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images-prod/originals/*. Add s3:PutObject permission on arn:aws:s3:::catalog-images-prod/thumbs/*, covering the 128, 256, and 512 pixel output sizes. The service sets a Content-Type header on each thumbnail, which requires no additional permission beyond s3:PutObject. Because the role and bucket share an account, the bucket policy requires no new statement. Validate by uploading one original image and confirming that three thumbnails appear under thumbs/ within a few seconds. A missing thumbnail usually indicates that the resource ARN in the PutObject statement does not match the output prefix.

A missing thumbnail usually indicates that the resource ARN in the PutObject statement does not match the output prefix.

This guide describes access for the EchoDraft transcription service, which reads recorded meeting audio in WAV and MP3 format from the bucket audio-archive-prod and writes transcripts as text and WebVTT files to the prefix transcripts/. The bucket and the service role, echodraft-worker-role, are in account 444455556666. The permissions come only from the role's identity-based policy, with no change to the bucket policy. Add a policy statement to the role that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::audio-archive-prod/recordings/*, since the bucket has versioning enabled and jobs reference specific versions. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::audio-archive-prod/transcripts/*. Limit the role to these two prefixes so that it cannot read other data in the bucket. Because everything is in one account, the bucket policy remains as it was. To test, start a job against a recording that is two minutes long and check that both the .txt and .vtt files are written. If the job reports a version-not-accessible error, confirm that s3:GetObjectVersion is present in the policy.

The permissions come from a bucket policy statement added by the bucket owner that names arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/echodraft-worker-role as the principal. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::audio-archive-prod/recordings/*, since the bucket has versioning enabled and jobs reference specific versions. A second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::audio-archive-prod/transcripts/*. Limit the principal to these two prefixes so that it cannot read other data in the bucket. Because the bucket is in another account, the grant is held in the bucket policy. To test, start a job against a recording that is two minutes long and check that both the .txt and .vtt files are written. If the job reports a version-not-accessible error, confirm that s3:GetObjectVersion is present in the bucket policy.

This guide explains access for the DocuMorph conversion service, which reads uploaded DOCX files from the bucket office-uploads-prod and writes the converted PDF files to the prefix converted/. The bucket and the conversion role, documorph-convert-role, are in account 555566667777. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy; the bucket policy is not modified. Create a policy with a statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::office-uploads-prod/inbox/* and attach it to the role in IAM. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::office-uploads-prod/converted/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of inbox/, so the service can poll for new uploads. The service writes each PDF using the source object's base name, so no rename permission is needed. Since the role and bucket share an account, the bucket policy does not need to reference the role. Verify with a one-page DOCX file and confirm that the PDF in converted/ opens correctly. If conversion jobs stay in a pending state, confirm that the ListBucket statement uses the bucket ARN without a trailing path.

The service writes each PDF using the source object's base name, so no rename permission is needed. Since the bucket is owned by another account, the bucket policy is the document that names the principal. Verify with a one-page DOCX file and confirm that the PDF in converted/ opens correctly. This guide covers access for the MarkSeal watermarking service, which reads product photos from the bucket brand-photos-prod and writes watermarked copies to the prefix branded/. The bucket and the service role, markseal-apply-role, are in account 666677778888. The grant is made in the role's identity-based policy only, and the bucket policy is unchanged. In IAM, attach a policy to the role with s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-photos-prod/raw/* and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-photos-prod/assets/logo.png, which is the overlay image. Add s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-photos-prod/branded/*. Do not allow writes to raw/ or assets/, so that the source files cannot be altered by the service. Because the bucket is in the same account as the role, no bucket policy statement is needed. Test with one photograph and compare the pixel dimensions of the branded copy to those of the source. If the service reports it cannot load the overlay, verify that the logo.png ARN is listed in the policy.

A second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::brand-photos-prod/branded/*. Do not allow writes to raw/ or assets/, so that the source files cannot be altered by the service. Because the bucket is owned by another account, the grant resides in the bucket policy. Test with one photograph and compare the pixel dimensions of the branded copy to those of the source. If the service reports it cannot load the overlay, verify that the logo.png ARN is listed in the bucket policy.

This guide configures access for the BundleRoute packaging service, which reads finished media assets from the bucket deliverables-prod and writes ZIP archives plus a manifest file to the prefix packages/. The bucket and the packaging role, bundleroute-pack-role, are in account 777788889999. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not changed. Attach an inline policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::deliverables-prod/final/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::deliverables-prod/packages/*, because archives larger than 5 GB are written with multipart uploads. Also allow s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so interrupted uploads can be cleaned up. The role does not need read access to packages/, since the manifest is generated in memory. With the role and bucket in one account, the bucket policy requires no edits. Verify by packaging a folder of ten files and checking that the archive and manifest.json both appear under packages/. If large archives fail partway, check that the multipart actions are present in the policy.

This guide describes access for the ClipMeta analysis service, which reads video files from the bucket footage-library-prod and writes metadata JSON sidecar files to the prefix metadata/. The bucket and the analysis role, clipmeta-scan-role, are in account 888899990000. The permissions are provided only through the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not altered. In IAM, add a statement to the role allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::footage-library-prod/clips/*. Add a statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::footage-library-prod/metadata/*, where each sidecar carries codec, duration, and frame rate fields. The service also deletes its own temporary files under metadata/tmp/, so include s3:DeleteObject scoped to arn:aws:s3:::footage-library-prod/metadata/tmp/*. Since both the role and the bucket are in the same account, the existing bucket policy needs no new statement. Confirm by scanning one clip and reading the resulting sidecar, which should list the correct duration. If temporary files accumulate, check that the DeleteObject statement is scoped to the tmp/ prefix.
